about: Synthetic company library and RFP-style questions for the retrieval evaluation (evals/retrieval.py). Each question lists the passage(s) that answer it. 'wording' says whether the question reuses the passage's words ('same') or says it differently ('different'). Written for this project; small, so treat results as indicative.

passages.label: Past proposal: Riverside Elementary
passages.text: Our firm built Riverside Elementary School, a 60,000 square foot K-12 facility for Riverside Unified, completed on schedule in March 2023 for $18.5 million.

passages.label: Past proposal: Oak Hill Middle School
passages.text: Oak Hill Middle School: a new three-story campus for 900 students, delivered under construction manager at risk for Oak Hill ISD in December 2021.

passages.label: Safety program
passages.text: Our experience modification rate (EMR) is 0.78, and we recorded zero lost-time incidents across 1.2 million work hours in 2024.

passages.label: Safety program
passages.text: Every site has a full-time safety officer. Crews attend a toolbox talk each morning, and all supervisors hold OSHA 30 cards.

passages.label: Quality control plan
passages.text: Our quality control plan uses three-phase inspections (preparatory, initial and follow-up) for each definable feature of work, with deficiencies tracked to closure in a log.

passages.label: Company profile
passages.text: Founded in 1998, the company employs 240 people and has completed more than 150 public projects across California and Nevada.

passages.label: Financials
passages.text: Average annual turnover over the last three financial years was Rs. 46.29 lakh, audited by a chartered accountant.

passages.label: Bonding
passages.text: Our surety provides single-project bonding capacity of $40 million and aggregate capacity of $120 million.

passages.label: Key personnel: project manager
passages.text: Pat Lee, PE, has managed school construction for 15 years, including six DSA-certified projects, and will be the project manager.

passages.label: Key personnel: superintendent
passages.text: Maria Gomez, superintendent, has run field operations on occupied campuses for 12 years and leads daily coordination with site staff.

passages.label: Schedule approach
passages.text: We build the baseline schedule in Primavera P6 using the critical path method and update it every two weeks with the owner.

passages.label: Occupied campus work
passages.text: When students are on campus, noisy work is shifted to evenings and weekends, construction zones are fenced, and deliveries avoid drop-off and pick-up times.

passages.label: Small business participation
passages.text: On recent public projects, 32 percent of subcontract dollars went to certified small and disadvantaged business enterprises.

passages.label: Local hiring
passages.text: We committed to hiring 30 percent of craft workers from the local community and partnered with the county apprenticeship program.

passages.label: Sustainability
passages.text: Four of our projects achieved LEED Gold certification, and we divert at least 75 percent of construction waste from landfill.

passages.label: Cost control
passages.text: We provide open-book cost reporting each month, track every change order against the guaranteed maximum price, and return unused contingency to the owner.

passages.label: Value engineering
passages.text: During preconstruction, value engineering on the Oak Hill project saved $1.4 million by switching to a precast structural system.

passages.label: Warranty and closeout
passages.text: At closeout we deliver as-built drawings, operation and maintenance manuals and staff training, and we respond to warranty calls within 24 hours.

passages.label: Credentials: license
passages.text: California contractor license CA-1043221, classification B general building, active through June 2027.

passages.label: Credentials: insurance
passages.text: General liability insurance with limits of $2 million per occurrence and $4 million aggregate; umbrella coverage of $10 million.

passages.label: Communication plan
passages.text: We hold weekly owner-architect-contractor meetings, publish minutes within two business days, and keep a shared log of open questions.

passages.label: Technology
passages.text: We use BIM clash detection before construction and give the owner live access to our project management platform for submittals and requests for information.

passages.label: Claims history
passages.text: The firm has not been debarred, has not defaulted on any contract, and has had no claims or litigation with public owners in the last ten years.

passages.label: Water infrastructure
passages.text: We have replaced 38 miles of water main for municipal utilities, including work funded by state revolving fund loans with American Iron and Steel requirements.

passages.label: Prevailing wage
passages.text: All crews are paid prevailing wages under the Davis-Bacon Act, with certified payroll submitted weekly through the owner's labor compliance system.

passages.label: References
passages.text: References: Dr. Alan Brooks, facilities director at Riverside Unified, and Karen Wu, capital projects manager at Oak Hill ISD.

queries.q: Describe your experience constructing K-12 schools.

State your bonding capacity.

Describe your approach to small and disadvantaged business participation.
Do you pay prevailing wages under Davis-Bacon?

Provide references from public school owners.
How will you protect children and staff while the school remains in use?
Describe your record of workplace accidents and injuries.
How do you keep the budget under control and report spending?
What did you do to reduce costs during design on previous jobs?
Explain how you plan and track the timeline of the work.
What is your firm's environmental and green building track record?
How many staff does your company have and how long has it been in business?
Have you ever been barred from bidding or sued by a government agency?
How will you keep the district informed during construction?
What will you hand over when the building is finished?

List projects involving pipelines for city water systems.
